title: Stooped bearded figure appears
html_source: This is the first of about a dozen protracted hallucinations that either Bloom or Stephen has in this Chapter. Here Bloom is confronted first by his father who accuses him of apostasy (a sin of which Rudolph is also guilty since he converted to Protestantism to marry Bloom’s mother) and then by a series of women with whom Bloom has been involved in one way or another. Also note that Rudolph assumes that Bloom is wasting his time with a drunken goy rather than realizing Bloom’s true purpose–to save Stephen.
